podcast.body: After a six-year hiatus, the Beastie Boys returned with this album. "The Beastie Boys came back after a six year absence with their To The Five Burows album."

srcs.episode: The 00's Part 3: The Return of Rock

podcast.body: Released after a six-year gap, this album served as a "love letter, and tribute to New York" in the aftermath of 9/11 and other global events. The album's creation involved a unique recording process where the band would start with beats, add rough vocals, and then, if a track sounded good, proceed to record final vocals using "fancy and nicer mics." "This album was really like New York City last, like everything has happened in New York City since like 2002, 2001, or whatever, you know what I mean?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This album was conceived as a love letter and tribute to New York City, reflecting the events and atmosphere in the city following the 9/11 attacks in the early 2000s. The recording process involved building tracks around beats, with band members contributing rhymes and then refining vocals with "nicer mics" before handing off to Duro for mixing. The album faced controversy in Europe due to copy protection software. "They call the album to the five boroughs."

podcast.body: This is a re-edition of "To the Five Brots," likely "To the 5 Boroughs," one of three Beastie Boys albums being re-edited on December 8th. These albums are noted as being among the most sought-after, demanded, and expensive in the Beastie Boys' discography. "se reditan tres discos en los bistiboyos que yo creo que son uno de los tres discos más buscados y demandados y más caros en encontrar de la discuracia de los bistiboyos, porque salen el To the Five Brots."
